title: Just Say You're a Wh$re - Raw Fusion #615 - Dating, Money & the Modern Marketplace
description:
One woman on TikTok says: if a man won't pay $300 for dinner, get out of the way — another man will. King B. heard it and lit the whole thing on fire. In this scorched-earth Raw Fusion episode, he takes on the modern dating marketplace where love has a cover charge and nobody wants to say what it really is: transactional.

From delusional singing-show auditions to the woman who auditioned for his own film and couldn't take direction, King B. argues that the real problem isn't the price — it's the dishonesty. He unloads on modern feminist dating advice, the "provider" language, and the sisterhood lies telling women they're all Ciara waiting on a Russell Wilson.

Provocative, uncomfortable, and impossible to ignore — this is the no-holds-barred relationship talk the dating podcast world refuses to have. Buckle up.

title: Why You Are Still Single - Raw Fusion #614 - Modern Feminism & Dating Reality
description:
She did everything right — the career, the money, the independence — and she's still single. King B. says that's not an accident. In this blistering Raw Fusion episode, he goes after the TikTok dating gurus cashing in on relationship chaos and the feminist playbook he says was never designed to get you a husband in the first place.

Using his infamous steak-versus-chitlins restaurant metaphor, King B. breaks down why modern dating advice keeps crashing: ignore what men actually want, demand old-school chivalry while rejecting old-school devotion, and call it empowerment. The result? A generation of women being coached into solitude by other women.

If you're tired of the same viral talking points and ready for the uncomfortable truth about modern dating, relationships, and why men walked away — this episode pulls no punches.

title: The Truth Had to Come Out - Raw Fusion #613 - Marcellus Wiley, Big Tigger & Relationship Accountability
description:
Two famous men. Two headline-making scandals. Two careers suddenly on ice. King B. wades into the legal drama and relationship wreckage surrounding Marcellus Wiley and Big Tigger — and he's not here to sensationalize it. He wants to examine what keeps going wrong when fame, money, and toxic relationships collide.

From messy divorces and custody battles to the facades people wear and the games both sides play, King B. traces the throughline: accountability. He argues that men stopped pushing back decades ago, letting modern feminist rules rewrite the game — keep the old protections, ditch the old obligations — and now everyone's paying the price.

This is the celebrity relationship breakdown with real teeth: no gossip, no moral grandstanding, just the raw truth about love, power, and the cost of ignoring red flags.

title: King B. TV Lands on Tonic TV + Roku - Raw Fusion #612 - Indie Streaming Takes Over
description:
King B. TV is going places — literally. In this episode, Tonic TV CEO A'aisha Fowler sits down with King B. to announce a new partnership bringing his channel to the Tonic TV Network on Roku, timed with the premiere of King B.'s ROOST: The Sequel.

But this is more than a business announcement. The two trade war stories from the independent film trenches — why King B. can predict a plot twist before the first act ends, why he deliberately watches terrible movies, and what the streaming revolution means for indie filmmakers who refuse to wait for Hollywood's permission.

If you're an indie filmmaker, a Roku cord-cutter, or just curious how independent TV networks get built from the ground up, this conversation is your backstage pass.

title: Billboard #1 Singer Sophia May - Raw Fusion #611 - Music, Mental Health & Mendable
description:
From diapers to Billboard — just months after giving birth, she hit #1 in America. Billboard-charting singer-songwriter Sophia May joins King B. from England for a conversation that moves from music industry war stories to something deeper: the mental health crisis nobody wants to talk about.

Sophia opens up about her rise, writing for legends like Gloria Gaynor, and finding herself more at home in Chicago's house music scene than in her own backyard. Then the conversation turns to Mendable — the mental health community and app she helped build — and why healing became the real mission.

Plus The Listening Party: King B. spins Sophia's tracks, including a rarely heard cut. For fans of house music, singer-songwriter stories, and raw mental health talk, this one hits different.

title: Alabama Luv - Raw Fusion #610 - Pap-Star's World Premieres & Kimberly Nelson-Zeigler's 'Figure 8'
description:
The bottom of the map is bringing the heat. Recording artist Pap-Star pulls up from Mobile, Alabama — the real birthplace of Mardi Gras, he'll tell you — for The Listening Party and two world-premiere unreleased tracks that show exactly why King B. had to have him on.

Then the tone shifts. Author Kimberly Nelson-Zeigler opens up about "Figure 8" — her autobiography of tragedy to triumph, dropping on Father's Day. From becoming a caregiver as a child to surviving abuse, she wrote the book she needed: faith in God, reaching eternity, and a lifeline for young women who've been violated and need to believe they can keep moving.

Two Alabama stories, one episode: Southern hip-hop heat and a survivor's testimony. Press play and turn it up.

title: Dying to Look 'Good' - Raw Fusion #609 - The Hair Relaxer Lawsuit Exposed
description:
She relaxed her hair for years. Now she's fighting cancer — and suing the companies that sold her the chemicals. In this urgent episode, criminal defense attorney April Preyar, Dr. Goldie, and hairstylist Tanya of Luxe Lab Pigmentation break down the national hair relaxer lawsuit linking chemical straighteners to endometrial cancer, ovarian cancer, and fibroids.

Who qualifies? How does the lawsuit actually work (it's not a class action)? What are the safer alternatives — natural hair, braids, keratin treatments with their own hidden dangers? The panel walks through the science of endocrine-disrupting chemicals, the legal roadmap, and why cases from across the country are landing in one Chicago federal courtroom.

If you or someone you love used hair relaxers for five years or more, this episode could change everything. Visit HairRelaxerHarm.com for the free qualification questionnaire.

title: PPP Loan Gone to Joint Custody - Raw Fusion #608 - Filmmaker Devon Bray's Family Business
description:
Nine hundred music videos. Two feature films on Tubi. One family-run production company out of Wichita, Kansas. Filmmaker Devon Bray stops by Raw Fusion to talk PPP Loan Gone and Joint Custody — and the grind that got them there.

Devon breaks down how he and his father shot their way up from music videos and wedding photography to festival runs and streaming deals, why he runs the whole operation as a family business with his wife, father, and mother, and the selfless mission behind his 200,000-member Facebook community helping other independent filmmakers get their Tubi films seen.

If you're an indie filmmaker trying to figure out the real business of streaming — or you just love a Midwestern success story — this conversation is pure fuel.

title: One Week to Cold N Windy - Raw Fusion #607 - Filmmaker Kenny Young's Chicago Story
description:
He went from child actor on Chicago stages to Columbia College film sets to a hit series on WeTV. Filmmaker Kenny Young comes home to Raw Fusion to trace the whole journey — and it's a masterclass in Chicago independent film.

Kenny breaks down his early days with creative partner Carl Seaton, the indie hustle of the early '90s Chicago film scene, and his series Cold and Windy — now streaming on All Black — a raw look at a female rap duo navigating the dangers of Chicago's drill rap scene and the music industry.

For aspiring filmmakers, Chicago creatives, and anyone who loves a come-up story told without the Hollywood filter, this is the episode. Real talk from a Chicagoan who's killing it on both coasts.

title: The Bizness - Raw Fusion #606 - Chicago Radio, Cannabis & That Girl Olivia
description:
Two Chicago powerhouses, one episode. Radio personality That Girl Olivia pulls up to talk about her rise on MyRadioChicago.com and Soul 106.3, the magazine she rebranded in the city, and the money tips that have listeners calling in to say her advice actually worked.

Then cannabis entrepreneur April Flowers — the show's official sponsor — breaks down her world as an infuser and event planner: the legendary Brunch and Blow, infused breakfasts, eight strains to sample, and full tours of the grow house from seed to sale.

King B. also gets personal about the health complications that paused his filmmaking run after five films and the comeback now in motion. Chicago radio, the cannabis business, and real talk — it's The Bizness.

title: King B.'s Hate…Love - Raw Fusion #605 - Da Wildcat Smith & J. Marie Go Raw
description:
He's been making Chicago laugh for years — and now he's starring in a Tubi hit. Comedian Brian "Da Wildcat" Smith joins King B. for a long-overdue conversation eight years in the making, diving into his name change, his journey through the comedy scene, and his starring role in King B.'s Hate…Love.

King B. also rewinds to the Last Laugh comedy troupe days, the Judge Mathis show moment that started it all, and why Da Wildcat is one of the few people in the business he calls a real friend — not just an acquaintance.

Then J. Marie steps in: model turned actress, Hate…Love cast member, talking about her leap from the runway to film and TV. Behind-the-scenes stories, Chicago comedy history, and a movie you can stream free on Tubi right now.

title: Vulture City - Raw Fusion #604 - Marcus Carothers on Surviving Indie Filmmaking
description:
King B. called it the Chicago version of Belly — and he doesn't throw comparisons like that around. Filmmaker Marcus Carothers, the star and director of Vulture City, sits down for a raw conversation about what it really takes to survive as an independent filmmaker in a city of vultures.

From shooting his own features to losing collaborators too soon — including a heartfelt tribute to his late friend Palermo — Marcus keeps it brutally honest about the hustle, the heartbreak, and the respect the game demands. (King B. bought his own premiere tickets. No freebies. Respect.)

If you're grinding in independent film, dreaming of your first feature, or just love Chicago cinema with real teeth, this episode is for you. Vulture City: the movie, the mindset, the mission.

title: King B.'s ROOST - Raw Fusion #603 - The Unscripted Review
description:
Nobody told Jason Schultz what to say — King B. made sure of that. The Nut Gallery's Jason Schultz drops by with an honest, no-setup review of ROOST, King's hit indie gangster film — a take King had never heard before the mics went hot. From there the two open the books on what it really costs to make an independent film: one man writing, directing, running camera and sound, casting the streets of Chicago, and starring as the hitman whose chickens came home to roost.

King tells the wild origin story — a five-minute director-contest short that fans demanded become a feature, because that love story was cool but everybody wanted the gangster movie — and how he scored roughly 60 percent of the soundtrack himself. The behind-the-scenes stories are pure indie gold: the historic Swift mansion secured because the actor managing it got cast, a crackhead hired the day he walked on set with Damn Fool, and lead actress Toya Turner earning the role of Sandy Calhoun in a mid-shoot switch. Plus King's directing philosophy: keep the set fun, keep it real, and build the performance in the edit. Essential listening for indie filmmakers and gangster-movie obsessives.

title: Cookie & Coop - Raw Fusion #525 - The Season Finale
description:
King B. closes the season with two of his favorite troublemakers. Pearl "Cookie" Reid and Ron Cooper — the stars of YouTube's "Dede and Odell: Senior Moments" — bring the laughs to the season finale, celebrating a combined four films written and directed by King B., from ROOST to Hate...Love.

This flashback is a taste of the finale's flavor: Cookie, Coop, and King B. cracking up over a fish dinner with the kind of unscripted chemistry only years of working together can build. The full episode is a hilarious send-off to the fifth season — press play, then catch ROOST streaming free on Tubi.

title: Professor Griff - Raw Fusion #524 - Truth That Got Him Shot At
description:
They shot at him. They burned his house down. He told the truth anyway. Professor Griff of Public Enemy holds nothing back in the most controversial conversation in Raw Fusion history — on mental illness, on the music industry's open secrets, and on why the people he came up with turned against him for exposing what he saw.

In this flashback, Griff recounts waiting a year for the pressure to come — and when it did, it came hard: gunshots, a torched home, former allies turned cold. The full episode goes further, into the Nick Cannon situation, his confrontation with DL Hughley, and the cost of refusing to stay quiet in an industry that rewards silence. Raw, unfiltered, and not for the faint of heart — this is Griff uncut.

title: Ben One - Raw Fusion #523 - "That Ain't Real R&B"
description:
A legend looked him in the eye and told him his music wasn't real R&B. Singer-songwriter Ben One — signed to Frank Thomas's Un-D-Nyable Entertainment alongside his brothers in the group Strong — opens up about the trials and tribulations of the music industry, the backstage disrespect, and why he smiles through it all.

In this flashback, Ben One relives the night at a birthday party when a major industry influence told him to his face that his R&B wasn't real — Southside to Southside. The full episode goes deeper: his rise, the group Strong, and three brand-new songs dropped live in the Listening Party. An R&B survival story with the receipts to prove it.

title: Tiny Thickemz - Raw Fusion #522 - Funny, Fearless, and Unfiltered
description:
Five kids. One shot of Jameson. Zero apologies. Comedian Tiny Thickemz sits down with King B. for a conversation as raunchy as it is hilarious — sex, comedy, and what it's really like to be a beautiful, sexy comedian running a show with no filter.

This flashback delivers her signature punchline in miniature: the bit about her five kids and where they "died" that leaves the room howling. The full episode turns up the heat with the uncensored stories behind the raunchy show, the grind of stand-up comedy, and why owning her sexiness is the whole act. Funny, fearless, and definitely not safe for work — press play if you can handle it.

title: Crea's Love Butter - Raw Fusion #521 - Love, Sex, and Radiant Skin
description:
Forty-two years old with the skin of a teenager — the secret is in the butter. Cre'Aye Williams brings her Love Butters to Raw Fusion for a conversation that blends love, relationships, and sex with a skincare ritual that's all about radiance. When Rose reveals she uses the Rose butter on her face for its antioxidants and anti-aging properties, the room does the math — and can't believe the number.

This flashback is a glowing taste of the full episode: natural skincare secrets, keeping that youthful glow, and the candid love-and-relationship talk Raw Fusion is known for. If beauty, self-care, and keeping it sexy are your love language, this one's for you. Find the butters at creaslovebutter.com.

title: Dr. Obari Cartman - Raw Fusion #519 - The Hood Is a Scientific Experiment
description:
The hood was never broken. It was designed. Mental health professional and author Dr. Obari Cartman joins King B. in preparation for the documentary Mental — with a thesis that stops the room cold: America's most struggling neighborhoods are the result of a scientific experiment, where poverty is stacked on poverty, resources are stripped away, dependency is engineered, and the fallout is studied for generations.

In this flashback, Cartman rejects the "wild kids" narrative outright: these are people who need healing, not cages — support, wellness, good food, clean water, the basic needs every human requires. The full conversation goes deeper into mental health in the hood, what we're teaching our boys and young men, and how men view women in our society. Challenging, compassionate, and impossible to unhear.

title: Wildstyle - Raw Fusion #518 - 25 Years After "Hay," a Message for Chicago
description:
Twenty-five years after teaching the world to smoke in the middle of the bar, Wildstyle has a message for Chicago's young Gs. The Crucial Conflict MC sits down for his most in-depth interview yet — celebrating the 25th anniversary of The Final Tic and the immortal "Hay," reflecting on working with legends like George Clinton, and testifying on what staying true really costs.

In this flashback, Wildstyle gets real about a city he barely recognizes: the youngers need mentors, the OGs need to bridge the gap, and everybody's out for themselves until it hits their own doorstep. The full episode covers the anniversary, the state of music, and a career built on never capping. An OG's testimony — for the streets and the studio alike.

title: Big Llou - Raw Fusion #515 - The Agent Who Launched Chicago's Stars
description:
She discovered Lisa Raye before the world knew her name. Singer and voice-over actor Big Llou opened Phoenix Talent Agency in 1985 — one of the first talent agencies on Michigan Avenue's penthouse row — and spent a decade launching Chicago talent into movies, music, and more. In this flashback she name-drops the future stars who walked through her doors as unknowns.

The full episode is pure free game: the good, the bad, and the truly ugly of the acting, voice-over, and music industries, plus hard-won tips for anybody trying to break in. If you're chasing a career in entertainment, Big Llou already ran the playbook — and she's handing you the pages.

title: BJay Johnson - Raw Fusion #514 - From Cable Access to CBS
description:
From a cable-access control room to the halls of 60 Minutes — and back to Chicago. TV producer and camera operator BJay Johnson traces a full-circle career: a Columbia undergrad mentored by broadcast legends Dan Rather and Ed Bradley, a professor shaping the next generation, and now a camera operator for CBS local news.

In this flashback, BJay tells the story of learning at the feet of the greats and carrying those lessons home. The full episode is packed with behind-the-scenes broadcast news stories and the kind of career advice you can't Google. For aspiring producers, camera operators, and journalism students, this is the blueprint.

title: Slique Jay Adams - Raw Fusion #513 - Crying in the Booth
description:
He never wanted to go solo — until the pain made him one. Singer-songwriter Slique Jay Adams started on Frank Thomas's Un-D-Nyable Entertainment, kept his stage name, added his real one, and turned tragedy into a prolific solo R&B career. In this flashback he asks the question that broke him open: how many children got to die before we wake up?

The full episode brings the Listening Party: hit songs, the inspirations behind them, and the story of a man who walked into the booth crying over his city and walked out singing. A raw look at grief, faith, and R&B as testimony. Press play — then go hear the songs for yourself.

title: Uncorked N Conversation - Raw Fusion #512 - The Sex Talk Nobody Has
description:
Ten, fifteen years in — somebody finally says the part nobody says out loud. Five women from the Uncorked N Conversation podcast join King B. for a candid, no-blush conversation about sex, love, and almost everything in between — including the mismatch nobody wants to admit: the partner who said "I can deal with it" early on, and can't anymore a decade later.

This flashback lands the uncomfortable truth from both sides — because men settle too, and plenty of beautiful, loving, caring women still leave their men unsatisfied. The full episode goes there on all of it: desire, disappointment, and the honest talk that saves relationships or ends them. Bold, grown, and unfiltered — pour something and press play.

title: Sean Whyte & Koolout - Raw Fusion Flashback #511 - The Future of Radio
description:
What happens when everybody has a mic and everybody has a show? Singer-songwriter Sean Whyte rolls through with his hit songs and a story about playing them for Montel Jordan himself. Then radio personality Koolout steps up to ask the uncomfortable question: with social media and podcasts everywhere, what purpose do radio DJs even serve now?

This flashback clip from Raw Fusion #511 is a short, sharp burst of real talk about putting the work in. Making a movie or landing a hit record looks easy from the outside — but the grind is the grind, and Sean and Koolout don't pretend otherwise.

A quick hit for anyone who loves music industry talk, radio culture, and the independent artist hustle. Press play and catch the moment King B.'s Raw Fusion was already calling the shot on where media was headed.

title: Intimate Friends - Raw Fusion #602 - The Sexy Film They Tried to Keep You From Seeing
description:
The cameras are off, the cast is in the studio, and the stories are finally coming out. King B. goes deep on his hit indie film King B.'s Intimate Friends — streaming free on Tubi in the US and Plex everywhere else — while co-stars J. Marie and Lerin Becton pull back the curtain on what it was really like to shoot one of the steamiest films of his career. Was it a true story? What inspired Eric and Brianna? The answers are in this episode.

Plus the debut of the brand-new Ask King B segment, where listeners write in and nothing is off limits. From the wild casting story of legendary Chicago DJ Herb Kent — discovered at a Sam's Club — to the spirit of entrepreneurship that turns an idea into a finished film, this one is equal parts seduction and business class.

Black cinema, independent film, and raw behind-the-scenes truth. Don't just watch the movie — hear how it got made.

title: Men and Women - Raw Fusion #601 - The Brutal Truth About What We Really Want
description:
Season six opens with the conversation nobody wants to have but everybody needs to hear. Live from Club Raw Fusion on Clubhouse, King B. sits down with mental health professionals Dr. Obari Cartman and Dr. Catherine Jackson for an unfiltered deep dive into male and female relationships — desire, honesty, self-sabotage, toxic patterns, and the one question that changes everything: do you actually want to be in this relationship, or are you just going through the motions?

The panel holds nothing back on monogamy, fear of being alone, and why so many couples stay in situations they've already quit in their hearts. But it doesn't end in blame — it ends in healing, with real steps toward reconciliation and relationships built on truth instead of habit.

King B.'s closing word says it all: men and women need each other. For anyone navigating dating, marriage, or the war between the sexes, this is required listening.

title: Cookie & Coop - Raw Fusion #525 - The Senior Moments Season Finale
description:
The season five finale closes with the two people who've been there from the beginning. Pearl Cookie Reid and Ron Cooper — stars of the YouTube series Dede and Odell Senior Moments — join King B. for a hilarious, heartfelt celebration of five seasons of Raw Fusion and four films made together, including ROOST, Hate...Love, and the infamous Penis Dialogues that started it all.

King B. reveals how ROOST began life as a five-minute short, why the DVD was called Roost 1-2, and how one casting idea turned into an entire cinematic universe. Cookie and Coop bring the laughs, the war stories, and the chemistry that only comes from years of making movies with family.

Independent Black cinema, behind-the-scenes storytelling, and comedy from two of King's day-one stars. End the season the way it started — raw, real, and laughing all the way.

title: Professor Griff - Raw Fusion #524 - Enemy of the State
description:
Strap in. This might be the most controversial episode in Raw Fusion history. Professor Griff — formerly of Public Enemy — sits down for a no-holds-barred conversation on Raw Fusion Live about mental illness, the music industry, and the culture wars nobody else will touch.

Griff draws the line between hip hop and rap, breaks down how food, music, and environment feed mental health, and speaks on the Nick Cannon controversy from his side of it — plus his confrontation with DL Hughley. The debate gets heated on protest culture too: when is marching just marching, and when does it become real strategy? Recorded in Chicago, delivered with the fire only Griff brings.

Hip hop culture, Black media, mental health, and industry politics — unfiltered. This is the one people will still be arguing about years from now.

title: Ben One - Raw Fusion #523 - Chicago's Smoothest Voice Takes Over the Listening Party
description:
The Listening Party is in session, and this week's guest has been killing it for years. Chicago singer-songwriter Ben One steps up to the Raw Fusion mic to talk about his journey — from signing with Frank Thomas' Un-D-Nyable Entertainment alongside his brothers in the group Strong, to the trials and tribulations of the music industry that he somehow smiles through anyway.

Ben One premieres brand-new music live on the show, including the undeniable "Bounce That" featuring Rio de Janeiro, pulled from his latest project The Platform. Then the conversation goes deep: what it takes to stay focused, stay real, and keep your soul intact when the industry tries to take all three.

Independent R&B, Chicago music scene, and an artist who looks in the mirror and likes who he sees. Tap in — the music alone is worth it.

title: Tiny Thickemz - Raw Fusion #522 - Tiny, Funny, Thick and Absolutely Unfiltered
description:
She's tiny. She's funny. She's thick. And she will say the thing nobody else will say. Rising Chicago comedian Tiny Thickemz sits down with King B. for a conversation that's equal parts comedy masterclass and pure chaos — from winning Best Sense of Humor in eighth grade to holding court on stage every Saturday night.

Tiny opens up about what it's really like to be a sexy, raunchy female comic in a male-dominated game: the hecklers, the butterflies, the grind of building a name show by show. She dishes on comedy war stories, including watching a fellow comic transform the second someone tests him from the crowd, and what it takes to own a room without asking permission.

Stand-up comedy, Chicago's comedy scene, sex, confidence, and laughing without limits. Warning: this episode bites back.

title: Cre'Aye Williams - Raw Fusion #521 - Love Butter, Bad Boys and Boundaries
description:
Love, sex, and the kind of relationship talk that leaves everybody a little exposed. Entrepreneur Cre'Aye Williams — founder of Cre'As Love Butter — joins King B. on Raw Fusion Live to talk about the business of beautiful skin and the business of the heart, from her radiant body butter line to why so many women keep choosing the bad boy over the nice guy.

The conversation cuts deep into modern dating: dominant women learning to step back, boundaries most people were never taught, and why society keeps mistaking aggression for masculinity. It's funny, it's flirty, and it's the kind of honesty most shows are afraid to touch.

Plus, King B. spotlights his mental health film fundraiser. Dating advice, women's empowerment, Black-owned business, and skincare that feels like foreplay — only on Raw Fusion.

title: Health of a Champion - Raw Fusion #520 - Defending Simone Biles
description:
When the greatest of all time says she needs to step back, the world should listen — and King B. has some things to say about everyone who didn't. Recorded during the Tokyo Olympics, this solo episode takes on the armchair critics who attacked Simone Biles for withdrawing from competition to protect her mental health.

This is a masterclass in what athletes actually carry: the pressure, the trauma, the impossible standards — and why choosing your mind over a medal is the real championship move. King B. breaks down how relationships, past wounds, and unspoken struggles show up in all of us, athlete or not, and why the stigma around mental health keeps too many people suffering in silence.

Olympics talk, athlete mental health, Simone Biles, and the fundraiser for King B.'s mental health film. Champions aren't just made in the gym — they're made in the mind.

title: Going Completely Mental - Raw Fusion #519 - The Talk Our Boys Never Got
description:
Some wounds never show on the skin. In this powerful episode, mental health professional and author Dr. Obari Cartman joins King B. for a conversation that goes straight to the heart of the hood — what we're teaching our boys and young men about pain, about women, and about asking for help.

King B. gets personal about his own battle with depression, the kind he didn't even recognize until he was deep in it. Together they take on the stigma that keeps Black men silent, the difference between "just crazy" and treatable, and why mental health is as real as any physical illness. This episode doubles as research for King B.'s documentary on mental health — and it shows in every minute.

Mental health awareness, Black men's wellness, depression, and healing. If this episode saves one life, it did its job.

title: Wild Style of Crucial Conflict - Raw Fusion #518 - Call of the Wild
description:
Twenty-five years after The Final Tic blew the doors off hip hop, Wild Style of Crucial Conflict sits down for his most in-depth interview to date. The stories are legendary: how a crew from Chicago's West Side came up with one of the cleverest album titles ever, the Mortal Kombat battles in the studio that shaped the record, and the anthem "Hay" — in the middle of the barn — that still moves a crowd like it was yesterday.

But the wildest part isn't the music — it's the man. Wild Style opens up about the streets he came from, pulling himself out, and why he spends his time now pouring real wisdom into the young people coming up behind him. Respect, roots, and redemption from a certified hip hop legend.

90s hip hop, Chicago music history, Crucial Conflict, and a conversation about the state of music that hits different.

title: So Much to Say - Raw Fusion #517 - Nichols vs. Taylor, Sha'Carri and the Culture War
description:
No guests. No filter. Just King B. and the microphone, and he has a lot to get off his chest. The ESPN firestorm between Rachel Nichols and Maria Taylor over a hot mic in a hotel room. Sha'Carri Richardson's suspension and the relay team snub that had everybody picking sides. And Simone Biles, the greatest to ever do it, getting King's full-throated support while the sideline critics pile on.

Then it goes bigger: the systems built to divide us, the attacks on people who look like him, and the pinky-finger truth about why healing has to start where the hurt is. It's sports media, culture commentary, and real talk from a man who refuses to sit quiet while the world spins.

Sports controversy, Black culture, media bias, and one voice saying what you're already thinking.

title: Bring Them Back - Raw Fusion #516 - Cosby, Sha'Carri & the Headlines Nobody's Neutral About
description:
Somebody's getting released, somebody's getting suspended, and nobody in the room is staying neutral. King B. brings back three Raw Fusion favorites — Malachi Gary of Inkful Thoughts Tattoos, Linda White of the Uncorked N Conversation podcast, and Mel Robertson of the ComicCool podcast — to tear into the week's biggest headlines: the Bill Cosby prison release, Sha'Carri Richardson's Olympic marijuana suspension, and the mental health conversation shaking sports after a tennis star bowed out.

The debate gets heated fast — media manipulation, accountability versus consequence, and why fame keeps colliding with the rules. King B. also opens up about his mental-health film "Mental," now raising funds, and why doing the work matters more than talking about it. Plus real talk for actors: how to choose roles without selling your soul, and why social media changed the gatekeepers forever. News, culture, and raw opinion — this is Raw Fusion unfiltered.

title: Llou's Blues - Raw Fusion #515 - Chicago's Casting King Spills the Industry's Secrets
description:
Chicago made him, and the industry couldn't break him. Big Llou — singer, voice-over actor, and former owner of the legendary Phoenix Talent Agency — sits down with King B. to pull back the curtain on the acting, voice-over, and music industries: the good, the bad, and the truly ugly.

From casting movies and stage productions in 1980s Chicago to an actor strike that rerouted his entire career, Big Llou drops decades of free game: why the audition is the actual job, why doubling as casting director and talent is a Chicago no-no, and how the internet changed everything for hungry artists. King B. trades war stories too — including starring as a ruthless record-label boss on his own soap opera while directing it. If you're trying to break into entertainment, this episode is a masterclass.

title: Flavor in Your Eyes - Raw Fusion #514 - From Cable Access to Broadcast News
description:
Before the PBS lights, there was cable access — and BJay Johnson was behind the camera. The TV producer and camera operator returns to Raw Fusion to trace the journey from grainy cable-access shows to broadcast news, alongside day-one stories of building Raw Fusion from nothing.

King B. and BJ talk the real business currency: relationships. Why keeping your word — and your friendships intact — lets you walk back into the game no matter how long you've been gone. They swap memories of Chicago's TV trenches, break down healthy ego versus the insecure kind, and BJ shares his gun-violence prevention PSAs through Real Appeal Media Productions. For aspiring producers, camera operators, and anyone building a creative career — this one's a blueprint.

title: The Definition of Slique - Raw Fusion #513 - Slick J. Adams, Steppers & Staying True to R&B
description:
Chicago steppers, stand up. R&B singer Slick J. Adams brings the Listening Party to Raw Fusion — spinning "This One's For The Steppers," "It's Your Body," and "Addicted" — while King B. digs into a career that started on Frank Thomas's Un-D-Nyable Entertainment label as a teenager from Englewood.

Slick breaks down why he added his real name to his stage name (a page out of the Sean "Puffy" Combs playbook), the tragedy that split his group and pushed him solo, and why he'll never chase trends — he's a singer, flat-footed at the mic, pushing R&B forward instead of copying what's hot. Plus the philosophy behind his smoothest records: a woman knows if she wants you the moment she sees you. Music industry real talk, Chicago style.

title: 1: Start Today — Your Journey Begins With One Step (Go Get It Minute #1)
description:
Waiting for the perfect moment? It doesn't exist. In the first Go Get It Minute, King B. delivers the truth about change: every great journey starts with a single step — and you're allowed to start small.

Stop staring at the mountain of zero to 100. Break it down: zero to five, five to ten, ten to twenty — and suddenly you're at 100. It's like a ten-hour road trip: overwhelming from the driveway, effortless once you're rolling. King B. pairs simple action with the laws of attraction to show why getting overwhelmed is the real enemy of every goal. One minute, one decision, one step. Start today, and let momentum carry you the rest of the way. Subscribe and hit the bell so you never miss a Go Get It Minute.

title: 2: Resolutions — Why Yours Keep Dying (and How to Save Them) (Go Get It Minute #2)
description:
Here's why your New Year's resolutions keep dying by February. King B. exposes the fatal flaw: most people treat change like a sprint, then abandon the whole thing the first time they stumble — and wait an entire year to try again.

That's not how transformation works. It's a marathon, not a sprint, and a slip-up only erases your progress if you let it. The new you isn't built on perfection; it's built on the refusal to stop moving forward when old habits pull you back. In this Go Get It Minute, King B. hands you the mindset shift that separates people who actually change their lives from people who make the same promise every January. Don't wait for next year. Keep going — right now.

title: 3: Set Goals — Write It Down, Date It, Go Get It (Go Get It Minute #3)
description:
Want a new life? Wishing won't build it — goals will. King B. lays out the next move after deciding to change: set real goals, write them down, and plant them where you can't escape them.

Vision board, smartphone, computer screen — wherever your eyes land every single day. Attach dates, not just dreams. Give yourself a clear course of action with deadlines, then work relentlessly toward the finish line. This Go Get It Minute is your reminder that clarity is power: when you know exactly where you're headed, every day has a purpose. So write it down. Date it. Stare at it daily. Then go get it — because a goal with a date is a promise you're making to yourself.

title: 4: Positive, Not Negative — Your Words Are Steering You (Go Get It Minute #4)
description:
Your brain is sabotaging your goals — and your own words are the weapon. King B. reveals the trap: repeat "I want to stop smoking" every day and you reinforce the smoking, not the stopping.

The fix is a simple flip. Stop naming what you're running from and start naming what you're running toward: "I want a healthier life. I want to breathe clean air." It's the elephant in the room — tell yourself not to look at it and it's the only thing you'll see. This Go Get It Minute turns positive self-talk into a daily discipline, because your mind follows your words wherever they lead. Aim your language at the goal, not the obstacle, and watch your whole attitude shift.

title: 5: The Beast — Unleash the Drive Already Inside You (Go Get It Minute #5)
description:
There's a beast inside you — and it's been awake this whole time. King B. calls out the quiet voice whispering "I don't know if I can do this" and answers it with the truth: the same drive that drags you out of bed for work every morning is the same power that can rebuild your entire life.

The hunger is already in there. The question is whether you'll focus it. This Go Get It Minute promises no perfect road and no problem-free journey — just the recognition that the beast within is strong enough to tear through every obstacle in your path. Yes, you can do this. Yes, you can move forward. Stop doubting the animal inside you and unleash it.

title: 6: Take Responsibility — Blame Is a Dead End (Go Get It Minute #6)
description:
Blame is a dead end — responsibility is the door out. King B. gets brutally honest: you can't always control what happens to you, but you always control how you react, how you manifest, and how you move next.

Stop pointing fingers at everybody else. Own exactly where you are — then forgive yourself for the mess and step forward making better choices. That's not self-punishment; it's self-respect, and it's the only foundation real change stands on. You don't control everything that happens to you, but you control everything you do about it. This Go Get It Minute is the tough love your life has been waiting for: take responsibility today, make the choices that put you in the best position possible, and build the future you actually want.

title: 7: Make Decisions! — Your Dream Life Is One Choice Away (Go Get It Minute #7)
description:
Your dream life is waiting on exactly one thing: a decision. King B. keeps it simple — you've dreamed it, you've set the goals, you've put them where you can see them every day. Now it's time to decide it's happening.

Want the car? The career? The new life? Decide — then go get the money, do the work, and make it real. Decisions aren't wishes; they're commitments that cut through every part of your life and don't take no for an answer. You'll make this kind of decision a thousand times, in a thousand different areas — so get good at it now. This Go Get It Minute draws your line in the sand: get crystal clear on where you're going, decide that's what's happening, and move like the outcome is already yours.

title: 8: Put the Work In — Faith Without Works Is Dead (Go Get It Minute #8)
description:
Faith without works is dead — so why are you sitting in a dead space? King B. closes the Go Get It Minute series with the final piece: you've taken responsibility, forgiven yourself, set your goals, and made your decisions. Now there's only one thing left to do.

Put in the work. Work hard, work smart — but work. Every faith tradition agrees on this core principle: belief means nothing without action standing behind it. This last minute is the call to get up, get out, and turn your dreams into reality with your own two hands. The plan is written, the goals are set, the decision is made. Now go earn it — because nobody's coming to build your life for you, and the life you want is waiting on the other side of the work.

title: Follow Your Dreams - Raw Fusion: Go Get It Minute #9
description:
Your dream won't chase itself. In this sixty-second shot of fuel, King B. breaks down why the first try almost never looks like the finish line — whether you're building a YouTube channel, breaking into the music industry, the film industry, or launching a business of any kind.

Results take time, and the ones who win are the ones who stay. King B. presses on the real engine of it all: passion. Get into what makes you want to get up in the morning, and refuse to let slow beginnings talk you out of the dream. A quick, punchy minute of motivation for creators, entrepreneurs, and anybody grinding toward something bigger. Subscribe and hit the bell so you never miss a Go Get It Minute.

title: Build the Business - Raw Fusion: Go Get It Minute #10
description:
Nobody is going to build your empire for you. In this Go Get It Minute, King B. delivers a blunt message for every entrepreneur working a day job while running a business: stop putting all your hours into someone else's company and letting your own go hungry.

Ten hours a day building somebody else's dream leaves your dream starving. Building the business from the ground up means putting real time into your own vision — whether you're scaling a startup, growing inside a company you love, or laying the first bricks of something new. A fast, no-excuses push for founders, side hustlers, and future bosses who are done waiting. Subscribe for more Go Get It Minutes — your business can't afford for you to skip them.

title: Sex, Lies & Podcasttape - Raw Fusion #512 - King B. vs. Five Women on Love, Lust & the Rules of the Game
description:
One man. Five women. Zero filters. King B. collides with the ladies of the Uncorked N Conversation podcast — April Brown, Tracey Langford, Paulette Irby, Serita Bostick, and Linda White — for a raw, two-hour conversation condensed into one explosive episode about sex, dating, and modern relationships.

Is marriage just a business deal with better lighting? Should a woman ever make a man wait? The room goes all the way there: down-low culture, the "think like a man" debate, the 90-day rule, why men turn dating into a conquest, what virginity language really says about women, and why sexual compatibility can make or break a marriage. King B. brings his unapologetic male perspective; the women push right back.

Candid, provocative, and funny — this is the relationship talk most shows are afraid to have. Press play if you're ready for the truth about love, lust, and everything in between.

title: The Future of R&B and Radio - Raw Fusion #511 - Sean Wyte Live Listening Party + Kool Out on What's Killing Radio
description:
The studio turns into a listening party. R&B singer-songwriter Sean Wyte steps in with a stack of records — "Kiss the Pain Away," "No Label," "Kisses," and "Body Language," the Montell Jordan-penned slow jam — and King B. doesn't just play them, he breaks them down track by track. The two go deep on what it takes to survive as an independent artist: writing your own songs, owning your publishing, and why the real money in music was never the show money.

Then the conversation flips to the airwaves. Radio veteran Kool Out (WGCI, Soul 106, WVON) gets brutally honest about the future of radio — syndication swallowing local voices, everybody with a mic starting a podcast, and whether quality can still rise through the noise. Two industries, one question: who survives the next era? A must-listen for music lovers, indie artists, and radio heads.

title: Hazel Maseko - Raw Fusion Flashback #510 - Reaching for the Life You Admire
description:
Every legend was once somebody looking up. In this flashback from Raw Fusion #510, guest Hazel Maseko opens up about what it means to study the people who made it — the ones living the successful life you keep Googling, the ones you quietly tell yourself you want to be like.

It's a short, honest moment about ambition: old scores, new dreams, and the hunger to build a life worth admiring. Sometimes the most powerful thing a guest can do is admit who they look up to — and why.

Missed the original conversation? This flashback is your invitation to go back and hear the full episode. Hit play, then dive into the Raw Fusion vault for the rest — and subscribe so the next flashback finds you first.

title: Coralyn Jewel - Raw Fusion Flashback #509 - The Hall Pass Debate
description:
Would you hand your spouse a hall pass? In this flashback from Raw Fusion #509, Coralyn Jewel wades into one of the spiciest relationship debates on the show: married couples — some together 18 years — who give each other a free Friday night to date someone else, then come home and trade naughty stories.

Coralyn calls it what it is: playing with fire. It's a sixty-second spark from a much bigger conversation about open marriages, trust, jealousy, and where the line sits between freedom and foolishness in modern love.

Want the full heat? The complete episode is waiting in the Raw Fusion vault. Press play on the flashback, then go hear how the whole debate played out — and subscribe so you never miss a minute of Raw Fusion.

title: Leon Rogers - Raw Fusion Flashback #508 - Who's Raising These Kids?
description:
The music gets blamed, but Leon Rogers points the finger somewhere else. In this flashback from Raw Fusion #508, the Chicago radio legend and actor takes on the culture war over explicit music: sure, the industry holds some culpability — but are you parenting your children?

His argument lands like a punch: the problem isn't the record, it's that five-year-olds are listening to adult records. A sharp, funny, no-nonsense minute on parenting, personal responsibility, and the music industry's favorite scapegoat. Leon Rogers holds nothing back — and the full episode holds even more.

This is just a taste of the full conversation with Leon Rogers. Dig into the Raw Fusion vault for the whole episode — it's worth every minute.

title: Lisa E. - Raw Fusion Flashback #507 - "Where Are Your Horns?"
description:
Some childhood moments never leave you. In this flashback from Raw Fusion #507, Lisa E. tells the story of a slumber party where a younger sibling — maybe five or six years old — looked at her and sincerely asked where her horns were, because the family had been taught that Jewish people were the devil.

It's a stunning little window into how prejudice gets planted early, told with the kind of honesty that stops you cold. One innocent question from a child, and a lifetime of ugly teaching behind it.

This clip is only the beginning. The full conversation with Lisa E. lives in the Raw Fusion vault — go hear the rest, and subscribe so the next flashback lands in your feed.

title: Steve Conley - Raw Fusion Flashback #506 - Tales from a Pittsburgh Steeler
description:
What happens when a former Pittsburgh Steeler walks into your workout? In this flashback from Raw Fusion #506, Steve Conley drops a story from his NFL days — the kind of gym tale only a pro can tell, complete with a football launched clean over the side of a car.

Short, wild, and straight from the trenches of pro football, it's a reminder that the best sports stories never make the highlight reel — they get told on podcasts like this one. Conley brings the locker-room energy and the laughs.

Want more from the former Steeler? The full episode is sitting in the Raw Fusion vault. Hit play on the flashback, then go get the whole conversation — more stories like this one are waiting.

title: Georgia Fort - Raw Fusion Flashback #505 - "Minnesota Is Racist as Hell"
description:
She had the résumé. Twelve years in journalism, two Emmy nominations, multiple markets, a college degree, board seats with the Minnesota Society of Professional Journalists and the Twin Cities Media Alliance. And they told her she didn't have enough experience.

In this flashback from Raw Fusion #505, journalist Georgia Fort names the systemic racism in Minnesota that the world only started seeing after George Floyd was murdered. It's a raw, fearless minute on what Black professionals face behind newsroom doors — and why the credentials were never the problem.

This is just the spark. The full interview with Georgia Fort is in the Raw Fusion vault — go hear all of it. Some conversations demand the whole hour, and this is one of them.

title: Malachi Gary - Raw Fusion Flashback #504 - The Tattoo Industry's Dirty Secret
description:
Think your tattoo artist is licensed? Think again. In this flashback from Raw Fusion #504, Malachi Gary drops a fact that surprises almost everyone: in Chicago, in Texas, and in most of America, tattoo artists don't need a license at all.

Out of 50 states, only about five to seven actually regulate tattoo artists and shops — a fact that surprises almost everyone who hears it. It's a jaw-dropping minute on an industry operating in the open with almost no oversight, and what that means for the ink on your skin.

Curious how deep this goes? The full conversation with Malachi Gary is waiting in the Raw Fusion vault. Flashback first, full episode next — and subscribe so you never miss a minute of Raw Fusion.

title: The Quad Squad - Raw Fusion Flashback #503 - The $2 Million Question
description:
Since COVID, these business coaches have helped companies unlock over two million dollars — money that was just sitting on the table because the business wasn't in order. In this flashback from Raw Fusion #503, the Quad Squad breaks down what separates brands that scale from brands that stall.

The keys: someone who holds your vision at all times, daily habits that program you for success, and a brand that stands out in the marketplace with real quality and credibility. Short, sharp business wisdom for entrepreneurs who are done leaving money behind.

Want the full playbook? The complete episode is in the Raw Fusion vault. Press play here, then go get the rest — your business will thank you for it.

title: Why Are Men and Women at War Over Love? - Raw Fusion #502 Flashback
description:
This 87-second teaser from Raw Fusion #502 cuts straight to the question flooding social media: why do men and women seem locked in battle over relationships? Entrepreneur Cinnamon Homes-Stovall sits down with King B. to hash it out — has one side been carrying the strength too long while waiting for the other to lead, or has nobody learned how to compromise?

The conversation takes a steamy turn with one provocative theory: couples who keep the passion hot might not have time to fight at all. If the sparks are flying, what is there to argue about — besides angling for a little makeup sex?

Get a taste of one of Raw Fusion's most talked-about relationship conversations in under two minutes. This flashback is only the appetizer — the full Love and Relationships episode goes all the way in.

title: The Money Nobody Told Small Businesses About - Raw Fusion #501 Flashback
description:
Sixty seconds that could change your business. In this flashback from the very first Raw Fusion episode, attorney and business strategist April Preyar breaks down how federal, state, city, and county governments — plus major corporations — were pouring money into small businesses to keep the economy afloat during the pandemic.

Her firm processed mountains of applications, becoming one of the city's premier firms for marijuana business licensing along the way. The message is simple: there is money on the table, and too many owners leave it there because their paperwork isn't in order.

Short, sharp, and straight from Raw Fusion #501. This is the teaser — the full Business and Law episode delivers the complete breakdown, from government grant strategy to cannabis licensing and everything in between.

title: Botswana Speaks - Raw Fusion #510 - The Africa They Never Showed You
description:
The commercials showed you huts and hunger. Botswana is about to show you something else entirely.

King B. goes international with Hazel Maseko, host of the Hazel Speaks podcast, broadcasting straight from Botswana. Hazel tears down the biggest misconceptions about her country, gets honest about the real relationship between Africans and African-Americans, and shares the powerful story behind her blog and podcast — born from surviving trauma and becoming a voice in the fight against sexual violence and toxic relationships.

And brace yourself for Botswana marriage law: get caught cheating, and the person you cheated with can be forced to pay your spouse damages worth thousands. Eye-opening, bold, and nothing like the Africa you were sold on TV — this is the conversation that connects two continents in one episode.

title: From Olympic Ice to the Sex Industry - Raw Fusion #509
description:
She trained to be an Olympic figure skater. She ended up running one of Southern California's biggest swingers clubs.

Born in South Africa and raised in America, Coral Jewel — adult performer, director, author, and host of the Hankie Pankie Podcast — pulls back the curtain on an industry most people only whisper about. She walks King B. through her unlikely journey: from figure-skating hopeful to production assistant behind the camera, to performing in front of it, to founding her lifestyle club and becoming a coach and motivational speaker.

Expect raw, honest talk about swinger culture — unicorns, hot wives, cuckolding, voyeurs, exhibitionists — and why consensual non-monogamy is really about community, not just sex. Mature, unfiltered, and not for the faint of heart.

title: Leon Rogers - Raw Fusion #508 - Busier Than James Brown
description:
Chicago comedy royalty Leon Rogers — morning host on WGCI, stand-up comedian, and star of "Later with Leon" on Fox 32 and Fox Soul — joins King B. for a no-holds-barred ride through his grind. The two rewind to how their friendship began, when Leon called up King B. about his film Intimate Friends and the late great Herb Kent.

Then the gloves come off. Who should inherit the Black Panther mantle — Shuri, Lupita's warrior spy, the Dora Milaje, or should the legend rest? They tear into the corporate "cultural vultures" running the music industry, and King B. lays out why TV is a formula while every film is a brand-new world. Laughs, hot takes, and Chicago media royalty — this is Behind the Mic at full volume.

title: The Woman Who Built Chicago Radio's Biggest Shows - Raw Fusion #507
description:
You think radio is just talking into a mic? Chicago radio legend Lisa E. — the producer behind some of WGCI's biggest top-rated shows — is here to set the record straight. Prep, research, credible sources, contests with real answers, games that can't get it wrong — and she did it all before Google existed to double-check her.

Lisa gets real with King B. about the grind nobody sees, her move into artist management with R&B singer Sean White, plus voiceovers, emceeing, publicity, and why credibility is everything in this game. Funny, sharp, and full of stories from behind the scenes. A must-hear for anyone dreaming of radio, podcasting, or the music industry — this is what it actually takes.

title: Inside the Helmet with a Pittsburgh Steeler - Raw Fusion #506
description:
What is it really like to strap on an NFL helmet? Former Pittsburgh Steeler Steve Conley — who played under the legendary Bill Cowher — pulls back the curtain on pro football: the Rooney family way, an organization that has had only three head coaches in its history, and what separates the Steelers from every other franchise.

King B. and Steve go full sports-bar debate: Chiefs versus Steelers championship dreams, Bears playoff hopes, pure Cowboys hatred, and the Chicago high-school glory days — football, track, and all — that built a professional athlete. Part locker room, part debate desk, all Raw Fusion. The game from the inside, told by a man who actually lived it — from Bill Cowher's locker room to Chicago Friday nights.

title: The Lies the News Tells - Raw Fusion #505 - A Former Anchor Confesses
description:
She used to read the news for a living. Now former TV news anchor Georgia Fort is telling you what the newsroom never says out loud: how stories get twisted, how coded words like "thugs" and "animals" get deployed against some communities while others become "stand-up citizens," and how aligning with bad actors corrupts the whole profession.

Fort breaks down why she walked away from the anchor desk to film her own stories with her own camera as an independent multimedia journalist — and she and King B. go deep on digital currency, global control, and the American decline nobody in the mainstream media will name. Uncomfortable, unfiltered, and exactly what the news won't tell you. Press play and question everything.

title: Tatted Up - Raw Fusion #504 - What Your Tattoo Artist Won't Tell You
description:
Thinking about getting inked? Listen first. Professional tattoo artist Malachi Gary sits down with King B. — who has zero tattoos and zero piercings — for the rawest tattoo conversation you'll hear anywhere: the good, the bad, and the ugly. Can you really catch a disease from a tattoo? What separates a shop you can trust from a nightmare you'll wear forever? Why doing your research matters more than the artist's portfolio?

And in classic Raw Fusion fashion, it gets realer than ink — about telling the truth even when it stings, because the friend who never tells you there's a problem isn't doing you any favors. Funny, explicit, and straight from a man who's been in the chair-side of the industry for years.

title: How to Fire Your Boss - Raw Fusion #503 - The Quad Coaches' Playbook
description:
Four business owners. One mission: make you more money. The Quad Coaches — April Preyar, Tiffany Taylor, Mel Roberson, and Andrea Thompson — join King B. to lay out their "How to Fire Your Boss" formula: find your passion, invest in yourself, do the research, and evolve your brand.

This crew has helped businesses pull in over two million dollars since COVID, runs multiple businesses between them, and knows exactly how much money sits on the table when your business isn't in order. If you're building something from scratch or stuck in a 9-to-5 you hate, this episode is your playbook — straight talk, real numbers, and coaching that actually moves the needle. Four coaches, four perspectives, one goal: more money in your pocket.

title: Love, Lust, and the Battle Between Men and Women - Raw Fusion #502
description:
Why does it feel like men and women are at war over love? Entrepreneur Cinnamon Homes-Stovall joins King B. for a steamy, no-filter conversation about modern relationships — from Gary Chapman's Five Love Languages to the uncomfortable truth about why people cheat in their 20s, 30s, and 40s for completely different reasons.

Guest caller Shawn DeJay drops a provocative take: women have carried their strength so long they've been waiting for men to take the lead. And nobody's dodging the hot stuff — passion, desire, and the fine art of makeup sex are all on the table. One of Raw Fusion's most rewatched relationship conversations, and it's easy to hear why. Steamy, smart, and honest about what really happens between men and women.

title: Where It All Began - Raw Fusion #501 - Business, Law & the NBA Bubble
description:
It all started here. The very first Raw Fusion podcast kicks off with King B. breaking down the NBA's return inside the COVID bubble — the giant virtual fan heads, the fake crowd noise, the Hunger Games energy — plus Colin Kaepernick, the kneeling protests, and why a true patriot defends the First Amendment even when the protest stings.

Then it's down to business and law: criminal defense attorney and Court TV analyst April Preyar answers the tough questions — her courtroom board game built from 54 real-life scenarios and seven principles, play-tested on 300 Chicago kids; marijuana business licensing; and why asking Black-owned businesses for the "hook-up" is the wrong kind of support. Sports, protests, money, and the law — history from episode one, and the blueprint for everything Raw Fusion became.
